title: Florida House, District 103
what_it_does: Represents District 103 (Part of Broward) in the Florida House; votes on state laws and the state budget.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); statuses Qualified/Unopposed only. Counties from the Legislature's district listings. Positions have not been researched yet.

candidates.name: Imtiaz Mohammad
candidates.background: Imtiaz Mohammad describes himself as an entrepreneur with an MBA and a community activist since 2015; he ran for the Florida Senate in 2024. His campaign emphasizes affordability, insurance costs and housing, and he says he would be the first Pakistani American elected to the office.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

other_issues.title: Affordability
other_issues.summary: Mohammad says affordability and cost of living are his top priorities but has not detailed specific policy positions; he did not answer the Vote411 questionnaire.

sources.title: Ballotpedia: Imtiaz Mohammad

other_issues.title: Affordability and cost of living
other_issues.summary: Mohammad said affordability and the cost of living are his top priorities and that the issue crosses party lines. He said his campaign focuses on practical solutions to rising insurance costs, the housing crisis, affordability, transportation and economic development, but did not describe specific policies.

sources.title: Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey - Imtiaz Mohammad

other_issues.title: Small business and public safety
other_issues.summary: Mohammad said he is committed to supporting small businesses, improving public safety and strengthening educational opportunities, and that he would represent all residents of the district.

sources.title: Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey - Imtiaz Mohammad

candidates.name: Robin Bartleman
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.occupation: State representative; former assistant principal and special-education teacher; former Broward School Board member
candidates.background: Robin Bartleman of Weston has represented the district since 2020 after serving on the Broward County School Board and Weston City Commission. A former special-education teacher and assistant principal, she holds degrees from FIU and Nova Southeastern University.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

property_tax.summary: Bartleman voted against both 2026 property-tax proposals and says Amendment 3 is a cost shift that could force cities to cut 25-40% of their budgets.
property_tax.quote: The bill sponsor stated that to make up for lost revenue, local governments can increase taxes and fees. That is a tax swap, not relief.

sources.title: Florida House roll call, CS/HJR 1-F (2026 special session), passage 75-26
Florida House roll call, CS/CS/HJR 203 (2026), passage 80-30
Vote411 Voter Guide (League of Women Voters): Robin Bartleman
CBS News Miami: Florida House advances bill that will clear most home property taxes

abortion.summary: She voted against the six-week law in 2023 and, in a CNN interview, described her own pregnancy decision and said the Legislature and governor did not belong in that room.
abortion.quote: Women are going to die because of this

sources.title: Florida House roll call, SB 300 (2023 six-week abortion law), passage 70-40
Media Matters: On CNN, Florida state Rep. Robin Bartleman highlights why Florida's 6-week ban will worsen the maternal mortality crisis

guns.summary: She voted against permitless carry and against lowering the long-gun age in 2025 and 2026, and filed a bill requiring police to seize guns from people served with domestic-violence injunctions.
guns.quote: The law already grants the judge the ability to say, you are too dangerous for a gun. This simply says, we're going to go get your guns now.

sources.title: Florida House roll call, CS/HB 543 (2023 permitless carry), passage 76-32
Florida House roll call, HB 759 (2025, lower long-gun purchase age to 18), passage 78-34
Florida House roll call, HB 133 (2026, lower long-gun purchase age to 18), passage 74-37
NBC 6 South Florida: Citing Tamarac murders, legislator wants guns taken when accused domestic abusers get injunctions

education_choice.summary: She voted against the 2023 universal voucher bill and says the school-choice program lacks fiscal and academic accountability.
education_choice.quote: The school choice program has limited fiscal and academic accountability; we must ensure tax dollars are not wasted and students are educated.

sources.title: Florida House roll call, CS/CS/CS/CS/HB 1 (2023 universal school choice), passage 83-27
Vote411 Voter Guide (League of Women Voters): Robin Bartleman

immigration.summary: Bartleman voted against SB 2-C, the 2025 state immigration-enforcement package.

sources.title: Florida House roll call, SB 2-C (2025 special session, immigration), passage 85-30

healthcare.summary: She passed bipartisan legislation expanding KidCare for working families and says she will keep fighting for affordable health care and prescription access.

sources.title: Vote411 Voter Guide (League of Women Voters): Robin Bartleman
Robin Bartleman campaign website

housing.summary: She supported the Live Local Act in 2023, co-sponsored the HOME Act (HB 675) and passed Miya's Law protecting renters.

sources.title: Vote411 Voter Guide (League of Women Voters): Robin Bartleman
Robin Bartleman campaign website

insurance.summary: She supported My Safe Florida Home and co-sponsored HB 319 to create a national insurance compact to spread risk and lower premiums.

sources.title: Vote411 Voter Guide (League of Women Voters): Robin Bartleman

elections.summary: She opposes HB 991's proof-of-citizenship rules, saying they create costly barriers and could remove eligible voters from the rolls.
elections.quote: I have consistently opposed bills that create hurdles for voters and citizen-led ballot initiatives.

sources.title: Vote411 Voter Guide (League of Women Voters): Robin Bartleman

growth.summary: She says she has been recognized by the League of Cities and League of Counties for defending home rule.

sources.title: Vote411 Voter Guide (League of Women Voters): Robin Bartleman

environment.summary: Her site cites her Unlawful Dumping law and opposition to an incinerator in the community.

sources.title: Robin Bartleman campaign website
